name: Salmon Recovery and Puget Sound Acquisition and Restoration grants

funder.name: Washington Recreation and Conservation Office (Salmon Recovery Funding Board)

summary: Annual Washington State grants to restore degraded salmon habitat and protect high-quality habitat, open to nonprofits, regional fisheries enhancement groups, tribes and others, ranked through local lead entities.

amount.note: Applicants may request any amount above $5,000; design-only projects without match are capped at $350,000

eligibility.rule: Project addresses goals and actions in a regional recovery plan or lead entity strategy
Not capital/public works, effectiveness monitoring, hatchery/harvest/hydropower, mitigation or eminent-domain/lease buys
Project is reviewed and prioritized by a lead entity

co_finance.applies_to: Riparian planting projects below minimum riparian buffer widths

documents: Landowner acknowledgement, for land the applicant does not own
Design materials; preliminary designs if requesting $350,000 or more
At least two photographs of site conditions
Applicant resolution and authorization, unless a Tribal sponsor
Riparian enhancement plan, for riparian restoration projects

deadline.text: Applications Due June 22, 2026 Applications Due by Noon.

amount.quote: Applicants may request any amount greater than $5,000. For design-only projects without match, applicants may not request more than $350,000.

co_finance_required.quote: A project with the primary purpose of riparian planting that does not meet minimum riparian buffer widths is required to provide 15 percent match.

eligibility.quote: Applicants must demonstrate how their projects address the goals and actions defined in the regional recovery plans or lead entity strategies.

documents.quote: Project Cost Estimate-RCO recommends using its template or similar format.
Landowner Acknowledgement-is required for a project on land not owned by the applicant or on state-owned aquatic lands.
Maps • Site plan for a restoration project • Parcel map for an acquisition project
Design Materials for All Restoration Projects. NOTE that preliminary designs ARE REQUIRED for a project requesting $350,000 or more in SRFB funds.
At least two photographs of site conditions before project implementation are required in .jpg file format.
SRFB Applicant Resolution and Authorization is required for any non-Tribal sponsor who will sign the grant agreement.
Tribal Notification Letter. This is required for all projects.
Riparian Enhancement Plan. Required for riparian restoration projects as primary purpose, regardless of fund source.
